steps.what: Clarify the geographical support request and intended use
Find relevant layers and check their metadata and permissions
Configure the requested geographical information product or application
Test spatial outputs and explain limitations in the deliverable
Deliver and explain the checked support product to the requesting organisation

tasks.design: Use a native layer catalogue and project templates in {OTHER}, the existing GIS application. The geographer configures and tests the actual support product, then delivers that exact version with its limitations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Layer navigation and repeated project styling consume support time.
tasks.enabler_now: Native metadata filters and compatible project templates support modest reuse.
tasks.still_hard: Intended use, incomplete layers and coordinate or licensing mismatches require judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Determine whether the result answers the request responsibly.
tasks.altitude: Reduce repeated GIS setup while retaining support accountability.

reach.learn: Preserve coordinate reference and date metadata

evidence.claim: Native GIS catalogues and project templates can reduce navigation and repeated styling; amounts remain unmeasured.

assumptions: This support portfolio produces existing GIS products, not a newly invented ticket report. No separate transmission beyond delivery in s5 is implied.
The geographer produces layer ID, revision, coordinate reference, resolution, date and permission status in s2; capture and validation time remain counted. Missing metadata forces manual inspection.
Catalogue filters remove 3 of 20 retrieval hours; project templates remove 3 of 30 styling/setup hours. Unique application logic and spatial decisions remain manual.
Ordinary same-system author saves remain retained without approval. Any system operation already automated today carries no labour saving.
unknowns: Share of support requests with reusable styles
research_questions: Can native filters and templates remove the specified operations on actual support requests?

already_counted.description: Test the product and communicate its limitations

incremental.description: Maintain catalogue filters and compatible project templates

approvals.approved_version: Exact tested product version, layers, recipient access and accompanying limitations; revisions invalidate the delivery decision

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 central B=100, R=94, gross 6 less 2 upkeep gives 4 net. Conservative case: incomplete metadata retains all 20 retrieval hours and only one template hour is removable; retain 99 plus 1 upkeep gives zero. For compatible output metadata and partially reusable styles, retain 18 retrieval and 28 configuration hours plus other 50 and 2 upkeep, giving 2 net. No generic percentage cut is applied across these operations.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Define the region, population and economic, political and cultural questions
Locate and assess sources on the population's characteristics
Interpret economic, political and cultural characteristics in regional context
Write the study findings with traceable supporting sources

loop.purpose: Turn the geographer's findings into explanatory prose
loop.input: Interpreted findings and selected supporting passages
loop.check: Geographer checks each claim, cultural qualification and citation against the source
loop.stop: One revision; unsupported claims are removed or written manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Explanations vary with the region and research question

steps.what: Check regional comparability, uncertainty and the final written interpretation

tasks.design: Use saved source filters in {DATA_PLATFORM} and source references in {DOCS}. A bounded drafting loop writes from the geographer's own interpretation; population comparability and cultural explanation stay human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated source navigation and prose assembly slow a regional study.
tasks.enabler_now: Saved searches and bounded drafting can assist these operations without substituting synthetic respondents.
tasks.still_hard: Changing regional boundaries, political context and cultural heterogeneity undermine simple comparisons.
tasks.human_edge: Interpret evidence in its social context and expose uncertainty.
tasks.altitude: Keep more attention on interpretation rather than source navigation.

reach.learn: Test representativeness and avoid treating regional averages as individual traits

evidence.claim: ASReview supports literature prioritisation; this capability does not establish the local retrieval cut.
Synthetic respondents can be less varied and drift, so they cannot replace population evidence here.

assumptions: The written findings are the study's existing working output. No extra publication or approval stage is added.
The geographer captures population definition, region boundary, source date, method and citation during s2; capture is counted. Missing comparability information is investigated manually.
Saved filters remove 7.5 navigation hours from s2, while all source assessment remains. Drafting assistance does not produce the interpretation in s3.
No population is inferred from synthetic respondents; ordinary author saves are retained without self-approval.
unknowns: Share of sources with comparable region definitions
research_questions: Does draft checking preserve cultural qualifications and accurately trace all claims?

already_counted.description: Review draft claims and final regional comparability

incremental.description: Maintain source filters and test drafting on changed source formats

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 central B=100, R=86.5, gross 13.5 less 3 upkeep gives 10.5 net. Conservative case: weak cross-region comparability requires all 30 source hours and extensive prose correction retains 18 writing hours; other 50 and 2 upkeep yield zero. With usable source metadata retaining 26 source hours and 15 writing hours, other 50 and 3 upkeep yield 6 net. Interpretation is fully retained throughout.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Analyze spatial distributions of physical and cultural phenomena

steps.what: Specify geographic scales, variables and defensible comparison units
Assemble geographic layers and validate dates, units and coordinate references
Calculate specified geographic distributions and summary measures
Analyze distributions, test scale sensitivity and interpret spatial patterns
Write findings and label maps with their analytical limitations

tasks.design: Use explicit GIS calculations and reusable import and map layouts in {OTHER}, the existing GIS application. The geographer checks layer compatibility and interprets distributions, then documents the findings in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated manual calculation, import setup and layout work sit between data selection and interpretation.
tasks.enabler_now: A specified GIS processing model can repeat known transformations without an agent.
tasks.still_hard: Scale effects, ecological fallacy and physical measurement differences require substantive judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish an artefact of boundaries or measurement from a meaningful spatial pattern.
tasks.altitude: Reduce mechanical calculation while preserving spatial reasoning.

reach.learn: Expose aggregation, projection and observation-date choices

evidence.claim: Explicit GIS processing models and layout templates can repeat specified calculations; the proposed labour effects are E1.

assumptions: The baseline includes 25 hours of actual manual calculation/setup to be replaced, not 25 hours of existing computer runtime. If already automated, those hours are ineligible.

The geographer supplies source revision, date, coordinate reference, variable units, aggregation key and method parameters in s1-s2, with capture and validation counted. Missing or incompatible layers are handled manually before s3.
Import presets remove 3 setup hours from s2; layout reuse removes 1.5 formatting hours from s5. Unique findings and map interpretation are fully retained.
This analysis ends at documented findings, without an invented publication send. Overlapping source assembly with 5511 is assigned once to the actual project.
unknowns: Compatibility across physical and cultural layers
research_questions: Can the processing model reproduce independently checked measures on different aggregation boundaries?

already_counted.description: Check and interpret spatial patterns and scale sensitivity

incremental.description: Maintain processing-model tests and coordinate-system compatibility

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 central B=100, R=70.5, gross 29.5 less 3 upkeep gives 26.5 net. Conservative case: incompatible layers retain all 25 assembly hours, existing automation leaves only 4 calculation hours removable, and unique output metadata retains all 15 writing hours; total retained 96 plus 3 upkeep gives 1 net. With compatible aggregation keys retaining 23 assembly, 9 calculation and 14 writing hours plus other 35 and 3 upkeep, 16 net remains. Each retained amount follows a distinct compatibility or baseline limitation.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop and maintain GIS software and equipment

steps.what: Diagnose geographical information system requirements and equipment faults
Develop software settings and device configuration for the diagnosed scope
Test candidate settings against spatial outputs and device behaviour
Apply the tested configuration to the operating GIS environment
Operate, calibrate and maintain plotters, digitizers, printers and cameras

tasks.design: Reuse compatible configuration templates within {OTHER}, the GIS application and its device management interface. The geographer diagnoses, develops and tests changes, explicitly applies the final tested configuration, and physically maintains the equipment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated connection, projection and device profile setup consumes development time.
tasks.enabler_now: Native exportable configuration profiles can reuse stable settings without autonomous deployment.
tasks.still_hard: Driver compatibility, calibration and unique hardware faults require direct testing and physical work.
tasks.human_edge: Diagnose the actual failure and decide whether the configuration is safe to operate.
tasks.altitude: Reuse stable configuration while preserving operational control.

reach.learn: Test GIS device profiles against reference output

evidence.claim: Compatible native configuration profiles can remove repeated setup; no local saving is measured.

assumptions: Hardware and software activities are a portfolio, not a requirement to service every listed device on each case. No new maintenance log is introduced.

The geographer produces device model, driver version, coordinate settings, connection parameters and candidate revision in s1-s2, with capture time included. Unsupported devices require manual configuration.
A reusable profile removes 5 of 25 repeated setup hours in s2. Unique software development, device tuning and tests remain. No benefit is claimed on deployment, existing runtime or author saves.
The s4 gate controls a real change to the operating environment, not a same-system save of the author's draft. Physical operations remain distinct from software work.
unknowns: Actual profile portability across the installed device fleet
research_questions: Which repeated device settings can be reused without recreating tests or introducing calibration differences?

already_counted.description: Test candidate settings and apply the selected operating version

incremental.description: Retest reusable profiles after GIS or driver upgrades

approvals.approved_version: Exact tested configuration revision, target environment, device models and rollback option; any profile or target change requires rechecking

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 central B=100, R=95, gross 5 less 2 upkeep gives 3 net. Conservative case: incompatible drivers allow only one setup hour to be reused; retain 99 and 1 upkeep gives zero. A partially portable profile removes 3.5 setup hours, retaining 21.5 of 25 configuration hours and all other 75; 2 upkeep leaves 1.5 net. Hardware and deployment labour remain fully retained in both cases.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Preserve spatial reasoning and reliable support while reusing known GIS operations.
reach: Work with surveyors on usable source metadata
Connect spatial interpretation with maintainable GIS products
skills_to_grow: Maintain and validate reusable GIS configurations
role.ambitious_version: A geographer who offers traceable spatial analysis and dependable GIS support with less repeated setup.
